paper_metadata.title: Genetically Engineered Quantum Circuits for Financial Market Indicators

summary: The paper demonstrates a 4‑qubit gate‑based VQSVD pipeline for estimating SVD entropy of a 4‑stock financial correlation matrix using GASP-generated state‑preparation circuits. Across target fidelities from 70% to 99%, the authors show qualitatively improved entropy estimation compared with qGAN and AAE state‑loading methods, with little accuracy gain above ~90% fidelity. Experiments use a 4‑qubit encoding of four stocks and four time steps derived from Yahoo Finance data (2008–2009).

experiments.description: GASP-generated approximate state-preparation circuits used to encode 4-stock, 4-time-step financial data for VQSVD/SVD-entropy estimation, evaluated across multiple target fidelities and compared against qGAN and AAE baselines on simulated and real gate-based quantum hardware.

algorithm.ansatz: parameterized state-preparation circuit generated by genetic algorithm; QSVD layers use single-qubit Rz/Ry rotations with linear CNOT entanglement
algorithm.convergence_criteria: target fidelity reached for GASP-generated state preparation; QSVD optimization performed for one layer
algorithm.parameter_initialization: GASP-generated circuit initialization; QSVD circuit parameters initialized as random values

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Stock-time return matrix a_nt loaded into a 4-qubit state |data> = sum_{n=1}^4 sum_{t=1}^4 a_nt |n>|t>; 2 qubits for stock index and 2 qubits for time index
problem_formulation.objective_function: Prepare |data> accurately enough that VQSVD can diagonalize rho_stock and estimate SVD entropy; LSVD cost minimizes Hamming-distance-based mismatch between paired stock/time bits
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: approximate state preparation via target fidelity; no explicit penalty terms reported

problem_instance.description: Monthly opening prices for XOM, WMT, PG, and MSFT over Mar 2008 to Mar 2009; repeated on rolling 4-month windows to compute correlation matrices and SVD entropy

dataset_specification.description: tickers: XOM, WMT, PG, MSFT; date range: Mar 2008 to Mar 2009; rolling windows used for Apr08-Aug08, May08-Sep08, Jun08-Oct08, Jul08-Nov08, and subsequent sections shown in figures

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: logarithmic returns r_nt = ln(s_nt) - ln(s_n,t-1); standardized into a_nt using mean and standard deviation; correlation matrix C_nm = sum_t a_nt a_mt; normalized so Tr(C)=1
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: comparison of ideal diagonalized-correlation-matrix entropy vs qGAN, AAE, and GASP across target fidelities; mean squared error of entropy and Frobenius-norm reconstruction error reported; multiple rolling time windows analyzed

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: compute log returns, normalize returns, build correlation matrix, generate target statevector
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: diagonalize reconstructed rho_stock / correlation matrix to estimate singular values and SVD entropy; compute MSE and Frobenius-norm reconstruction error

convergence_data.loss_curve_shape: shown for example runs; decreasing loss during optimization

speedup_claims.caveats: The paper does not claim a formal asymptotic or empirical speedup. It states that GASP circuits have low depth and are feasible on real hardware, but no quantified speedup over classical or alternative quantum methods is provided.

advantage_assessment.crossover_size: unknown; experiment demonstrated only for a 4-qubit problem (4 assets × 4 time steps)
advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Not analyzed in the paper. Scaling would require significantly more qubits to encode larger asset-time matrices and deeper circuits for VQSVD training.
limiting_factors: extremely small problem size (4 assets, 4 time steps)
no runtime or complexity comparison against classical SVD
